nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Summer sun and long dry spells shape which trees and shrubs can thrive on the slopes.

nodes.name: Winter rain and snow
nodes.desc: Most of the range's precipitation falls in winter; around 790 mm a year at Prodromos on the high slopes.

nodes.name: Troodos rock and thin soil
nodes.desc: The massif is an uplifted slab of ancient oceanic crust; the golden oak is restricted to its igneous rocks.

nodes.name: Turkish pine
nodes.desc: Covers about 175,000 hectares of Cyprus, roughly 90% of its woodland, and is the most important forestry tree.

nodes.name: Anatolian black pine
nodes.desc: The Cyprus form of black pine forms forests on the higher slopes, alongside junipers.

nodes.name: Golden oak
nodes.desc: Endemic to Cyprus; the main broadleaved tree of the conifer forests. Its stands hold soil on stony slopes and build humus.

nodes.name: Grasses and herbs
nodes.desc: Understory grasses and wildflowers growing between trees and in clearings.

nodes.name: Cyprus mouflon
nodes.desc: Endangered wild sheep, the national animal of Cyprus, living in the mountains of Paphos District. Eats leaves and grasses.

nodes.name: Red crossbill
nodes.desc: Finch with a crossed bill adapted to prise seeds out of conifer cones; recorded in large numbers in the pine forests.

nodes.name: Eurasian jay
nodes.desc: Woodland crow that feeds heavily on acorns, as well as insects and other foods.

nodes.name: Common wood pigeon
nodes.desc: Large pigeon eating seeds, acorns, buds and leaves; a main prey of Bonelli's eagle on Cyprus.

nodes.name: Black rat
nodes.desc: Introduced omnivorous rodent eating seeds and fruit; second most common prey of Bonelli's eagle in a Cyprus diet study.

nodes.name: Large White butterfly
nodes.desc: Butterfly whose caterpillars eat the leaves of herbs; adults and larvae feed insect-eating birds and lizards.

nodes.name: Short-toed treecreeper
nodes.desc: Small bark-creeping bird recorded in large numbers; GloBI records it eating butterflies such as the large white.

nodes.name: Cyprus wheatear
nodes.desc: Breeds only on Cyprus, often in woodland. Hunts insects and, in GloBI records, small lizards.

nodes.name: Masked shrike
nodes.desc: Eats mostly large insects, occasionally small vertebrates, and impales prey on thorns. Breeds on Cyprus.

nodes.name: Cypriote wall lizard
nodes.desc: Lizard endemic to Cyprus found from sea level to about 1,600 m; needs shade. A prey of many birds and snakes.

nodes.name: Cyprus whip snake
nodes.desc: Endemic to Cyprus and widespread in Troodos; eats lizards, amphibians, insects and other snakes.

nodes.name: Eurasian griffon vulture
nodes.desc: Feeds mainly on carrion. Lives among the crags of the range and cleans up dead animals.

nodes.name: Bonelli's eagle
nodes.desc: Cyprus diet studies show it taking chukar, pigeons, black rats, jackdaws and lizards, mostly caught alive.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Opportunistic omnivore eating birds, reptiles, rodents, fruit and carrion.

nodes.name: Soil fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down pine needles, oak leaves and carcasses; oak partners with fungi in the soil.
